summary.text: A 76-year-old man presented with dyspnea on exertion, classified as Hugh-Jones 2, after consulting his family doctor six months earlier, when a chest X-ray raised suspicion of interstitial lung disease. He was referred six months after symptom onset. He was a current smoker with 30 packs/year and a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease treated with a proton pump inhibitor, and was also aware of edema and Raynaud's phenomenon.

Examination showed skin thickening with a Rodnan score of 27, fine crackles in both lower back regions and mild pitting edema of both lower legs. Chest CT showed a subpleural reticular pattern, traction bronchiectasis and consolidation, and spirometry showed a reduced forced vital capacity of 2.13 L. Anti-Scl-70 and anti-centromere antibodies were negative while anti-eIF2B and anti-SS-A/Ro52 were positive, and BALF eosinophils were increased.

A collagen specialist was consulted immediately after the visit, and mixed connective tissue disease and Sjögren's syndrome were initially considered. After investigation of minor antibodies he was diagnosed with interstitial lung disease and diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis positive for anti-eIF2B antibodies, with a probable UIP pattern on chest CT.

The collagen specialist judged immunosuppressive drugs such as mycophenolate and steroids not indicated at this stage, so nintedanib was administered and he was followed up at the hospital. A whole-body CT performed as a screening showed no findings suspicious for cancer.

article_limitations: Table 4 lists published literature cases; only its present-case row concerns the index patient, and its gastric involvement and renal disease cells are kept review-only because the 0/1 convention is undefined.
Discussion sentences about cohorts, mechanisms and published studies are background, not patient facts.
The case text gives no calendar dates; the only relative times are six months ago, six months after symptom onset, immediately after the visit and initially.
No outcome after nintedanib is reported, so no outcomes are recorded.
